$comment: Update scenarios that the Azure Functions canvas shows and starts. This file is the source of truth: do not add a scenario in the canvas code. status: available (the reference file of this skill gives the steps, and the SKILL.md table links it), planned (shown, but the user cannot start it; reference is null), or external (a skill in another plugin does the work; skill names it, and reference is null). from: the project facts that show that the scenario applies. A list value means any of these values. programmingModel and hostingPlan are keys in lifecycle.json; extensionBundle is the major version of host.json extensionBundle. A scenario with no from is never detected; the user selects it. validatedFrameworks (optional): the TFMs for which this scenario's Definition of done has actual build/test/E2E evidence. Add a TFM here only after the reference file's frameworkRevalidationSection actually ran and passed for it; never add it only because a project now targets it. frameworkRevalidationSection (optional, needs validatedFrameworks): the heading in the reference file to redo when a project's TargetFramework later changes outside this scenario (for example, by a separate .NET upgrade tool). azure-functions-doctor's MG-001 reads both fields; do not copy Definition of done IDs or text into the doctor skill. docs/checks.md must agree; test/unit/check-catalog.test.mjs checks it.
